class.name: PlayerController
class.brief_description: A human's controller: it possesses a pawn and owns that player's input.
class.description: It exists on the server for every player and on each client for that client's own player, and nowhere else - which is what makes it the right place to send a player's input from, and the wrong place to keep anything everyone has to see. On possession it calls [code]_setup_input_component[/code] on the [Pawn], which is where input actions get bound, and makes the pawn camera current where the player is actually sitting. It belongs to a level and dies with it. The human behind it is the [LocalPlayer], which the [GameInstance] owns and which survives [method World.load_level] - that is where the device assignment and the split screen viewport live. In a networked game the owning client sends what its player is holding and the server applies it to this controller's [PlayerInput], so the input component and the pawn run the same code in every net mode. Input from any peer other than [method Controller.get_owner_peer_id] is dropped.

method.name: get_player_viewport
method.description: [member LocalPlayer.viewport_override] if the player has one, otherwise this node viewport.

method.name: is_local_player_controller
method.description: Always true today. The hook exists so code written now stays correct once a client owns only a subset of the world controllers.

method.name: register_input_component
method.description: Adds the component to this controller input stack and points it at this controller, which is how it finds the right [PlayerInput].
